definition: The process of releasing new software to servers or users.
exampleSentence: The team scheduled the deployment for Saturday night to avoid disturbing customers.

definition: A central place where code and its history are stored.
exampleSentence: All of our source files are stored in a private repository on GitHub.

definition: A version of software that is made available to users.
exampleSentence: The next release will include a dark mode and faster search.

definition: A separate line of development in version control.
exampleSentence: Create a new branch before you start working on the login feature.

definition: A saved set of changes in version control.
exampleSentence: Write a clear message for every commit so others understand your changes.

definition: Combining the changes from one branch into another.
exampleSentence: The merge failed because two developers changed the same line.

definition: A request to review and merge your code changes.
exampleSentence: Please open a pull request when your feature is ready for review.

definition: When other developers check your code before it is merged.
exampleSentence: The code review found a security problem before the update went live.

definition: A small automatic test that checks one part of the code.
exampleSentence: Every new function should come with at least one unit test.

definition: A library or service that your code needs in order to work.
exampleSentence: An outdated dependency caused the build to fail this morning.

definition: The settings that control how a system works.
exampleSentence: A small mistake in the configuration stopped the server from starting.

definition: Written guides that explain how software works or how to use it.
exampleSentence: Good documentation helps new employees understand the system quickly.

definition: A separate setup for running software, such as test or production.
exampleSentence: Always test your changes in the staging environment before going live.

definition: Extra future work caused by choosing a quick solution now.
exampleSentence: Skipping tests to meet deadlines creates technical debt that slows the team later.

definition: A list of tasks and features that are waiting to be done.
exampleSentence: The product owner added five new tasks to the backlog today.

definition: A short, fixed period in which a team completes planned work.
exampleSentence: Our team plans its work in two-week sprint cycles.

definition: A recorded request for help or for a task in a tracking system.
exampleSentence: Please create a ticket if your laptop needs to be repaired.

definition: The team that answers employees' or customers' technical questions.
exampleSentence: Call the help desk if you cannot connect to the company VPN.

definition: A period when a service or system stops working.
exampleSentence: A power outage took the company website offline for two hours.

definition: Time when a system is not available.
exampleSentence: The update caused ten minutes of downtime during the night.

definition: Time when a system is working and available.
exampleSentence: Our hosting provider promises 99.9 percent uptime every month.

definition: A system that shares traffic between several servers.
exampleSentence: The load balancer sends each visitor to the least busy server.

definition: A server that sits between users and the internet.
exampleSentence: All office traffic goes through a proxy that blocks dangerous websites.

definition: A device that connects two different networks.
exampleSentence: The gateway connects our office network to the internet.

definition: The slowest part of a system, which limits its speed.
exampleSentence: The old database server is the main bottleneck in our system.

definition: An unexpected event that disrupts a service or its security.
exampleSentence: The security team is investigating an incident from last night.

definition: When attackers get into a system and access private data.
exampleSentence: The data breach exposed the email addresses of thousands of customers.

definition: The username and password used to log in.
exampleSentence: Never share your login credentials with anyone, even with colleagues.

definition: Malware that locks your files and asks for money to unlock them.
exampleSentence: Regular backups protect the company if ransomware locks our files.

definition: Rules that decide who can use which systems or data.
exampleSentence: Strict access control means interns cannot see salary data.

definition: An official check of systems, records or security.
exampleSentence: The external audit checks whether we follow security rules.

definition: Following laws, rules and company policies.
exampleSentence: Our compliance team makes sure we follow data protection laws.

definition: A planned attack by experts to find security weaknesses.
exampleSentence: The penetration test showed that our admin page was easy to attack.

definition: A screen that shows important data and charts in one place.
exampleSentence: The sales dashboard shows today's orders and revenue in real time.

definition: The study of data to find useful patterns.
exampleSentence: Website analytics show that most visitors use their phones.

definition: Numbers used to measure performance.
exampleSentence: The team reviews its key metrics every Monday morning.

definition: The ability of a system to handle more users or data.
exampleSentence: Moving to the cloud improved the scalability of our online shop.

definition: Moving data from one system to another.
exampleSentence: The data migration to the new system took the whole weekend.

definition: A powerful desk computer used for professional work.
exampleSentence: Designers in our office use a workstation with two large monitors.

definition: A device that connects a laptop to monitors, a keyboard and a network.
exampleSentence: Plug your laptop into the docking station to use both screens.
